title: A normalized two point extremizer
statement: Let $p,\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $1<p<2$, $0<\alpha<\beta$, and $\alpha^p+\beta^p=1$. Set $u=\beta/\alpha$, $v=\alpha/\beta$, and $r=(\alpha^p\beta^{2-p}-\alpha^{2-p}\beta^p)/(\alpha^2-\beta^2)$. Then $u\ne v$, $\alpha^p u^p+\beta^p v^p=1$, and $(\alpha^p u+\beta^p v)^2+r\alpha^p\beta^p(u-v)^2=1$.
replaced: Let $1<p<2$, $0<\alpha<\beta$, and $\alpha^p+\beta^p=1$. Put $r=(\alpha^p\beta^{2-p}-\alpha^{2-p}\beta^p)/(\alpha^2-\beta^2)$. For $u=\beta/\alpha$ and $v=\alpha/\beta$, one has $u\ne v$, $\alpha^pu^p+\beta^pv^p=1$, and $(\alpha^pu+\beta^pv)^2+r\alpha^p\beta^p(u-v)^2=1$.
